newsitem.title: CROATIA: Orthodox leader urges Serbs to stay, vote.
newsitem.headline: Orthodox leader urges Serbs to stay, vote.

text.p: A leader of Serbia's influential Orthodox Church urged the Serbs in Eastern Slavonia on Tuesday to stay in their homes and vote in local elections ahead of the region's return to Croatian rule due this summer.

Eastern Slavonia is the last Serb enclave in Croatia. Its reintegration with the rest of the country will peacefully end a six-year conflict that started when minority Serbs opposing Croatia's independence carved out their own mini state in 1991.

In a statement faxed to Reuters, Metropolitan Jovan, whose diocese covers Serbs in Croatia, Slovenia and Italy, also called on Zagreb authorities to show tolerance and understanding while bringing about the reintegration.
"We are calling on all the faithful who live in those areas not to leave their homes, to take part in the election and thus show their political will," the statement said.

Of some 120,000 Serbs living in the enclave, roughly half are refugees from other rebel enclaves Zagreb recaptured in 1995. They will take part in the voting for the first time since their 1991 rebellion.

The U.N. administration of the area expects up to 20 percent will flee to nearby Serbia before Croatian refugees and police return. Serb leaders put the number of those unwilling to accept Croatian rule at 50 percent or more.
They decided last week to hold a referendum on April 6 as to whether Eastern Slavonia should remain territorially united after reintegration.
Croatia wants to divide the area in two counties.
